directions.name: From calling to launch Sunday
directions.angle: The planter's journey through the seven church phases. The planter is the hero. Sending churches and networks appear as the people who walk beside the planter.

hero.headline: From calling to launch Sunday.
hero.subhead: Keep your people, gatherings, follow-ups and teams in one place as your core team and launch team grow toward launch Sunday.

problem.headline: A church launch has a hundred moving parts. Most of them live in your head.
problem.body: Three guests came to Thursday's vision meeting, and someone needs to follow up with them by Saturday. Commitment cards sit in a folder. The kids ministry still has no leader. Your spreadsheet knows none of this, so the loudest problem gets your week, not the most important one.

proof.headline: Here is what a Monday looks like.
proof.body: Your core team and your launch team, and how both are growing. When your last vision meeting was, and when the next one is. Late follow-ups and who owns each one. One focus from Plant Intelligence, with the facts it used.
proof.visual: Overview dashboard from the round-buffalo mockup: Core group, Vision meetings, Where people are, Coming up, Focus this week and Needs you.

features.headline: Everything a plant needs, in the order you need it.

items.label: Phase 0 · Discovery
items.title: Start with clear guidance
items.body: Everyfield opens the guidance for the phase you are in, so you read what matters now.

items.label: Phase 1 · Core group
items.title: Grow a committed core group
items.body: Track each person from first visit to signed commitment. Record interviews against the five considerations and the 4 Cs. When you close a vision meeting's attendance, Everyfield creates the follow-up tasks.

items.label: Phase 2 · Launch team
items.title: Set the date and fill the roles
items.body: Set launch day. See which of the eight ministry areas still has no leader, and who on your core group has the skills for it.

items.label: Phase 3 · Training
items.title: Train every team
items.body: Plan training meetings for each ministry team and see who has finished.

items.label: Phase 4 · Pre-launch
items.title: Finish the launch list
items.body: Work through launch milestones and their tasks. Send email to your people and print documents that already carry your church's details.

items.label: Phases 5 and 6 · Launch and after
items.title: Launch, then keep going
items.body: Record Launch Sunday and its outcome. Keep follow-up running when Sunday becomes a weekly rhythm.

evry.headline: Evry prepares the work. You approve it.
evry.body: Ask Evry who from last Thursday has no follow-up yet. It shows the list, with a link to each person. Ask it to follow up, and it creates a task for each guest, assigns it to someone on your core team and drafts what to say. Nothing is saved until you approve the exact change on screen.

example.ask: Who from Thursday's vision meeting has no follow-up owner?
example.answer: Three first-time guests have no follow-up owner yet.
example.review: Review 3 changes · Assign follow-up tasks · Approve or Edit

evry.limits: Evry does not write prayers, give counsel, judge a person's readiness or change your phase. It never reads your private check-in.

directions.angle: The sending church or network that needs honest visibility into many plants. The buyer is the hero. The planter's daily tool is the reason the data is real, and consent is the reason planters accept it.

hero.subhead: See the phase, health and launch readiness of each plant that shares with you. Never their people.

problem.headline: You usually hear about a struggling plant when it is already late.
problem.body: Reports come once a quarter, and each planter writes them a different way. A plant can go a month without a vision meeting before anyone outside notices. Coaches spend the first half of each meeting finding out what happened.

proof.headline: One row for each plant. One status you can act on.
proof.body: Each plant shows its phase, launch date and a health status: on track, watch, launch readiness or limited visibility. Limited visibility means the plant shares too little for a fair read.
proof.visual: Oversight table: plant name, phase track, launch date, status badge. Use the mockup's StatusBadge and PhaseTrack components.

evry.headline: Planters get an assistant that does the busywork.
evry.body: Evry works inside the plant's account. It finds records, drafts follow-up tasks and emails, and explains a Plant Intelligence result against the rubric. Every change waits for the planter's approval, so the records your summary comes from stay the planter's own work.

example.ask: Why does Plant Intelligence say my follow-up is slipping?
example.answer: Twelve people have a follow-up task that is past its due date. Here they are, with the date each one was last contacted.
example.review: Review 12 changes · Assign follow-up tasks · Approve or Edit

evry.limits: Evry is for the plant team. It does not give sending churches or networks extra access, and it never reads a planter's private check-in.
